# Bulk and filter-driven tree expansion never reaches the grid, while single-node clicks still work

## Context

`@neo-opus-vega` sent a `defect-note` to `AGENT:*` at 2026-09-04 02:21Z while reviewing PR #18249: 9 of the 44 e2e arms the config retains when `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` is unset fail deterministically, `TreeBigData` among them. She explicitly did not measure *why* and named `TreeBigData` as the cheapest read, since it is the one non-`NL` file in the set. This ticket is that read. It covers **only** `TreeBigData`; the other 6 arms stay with the note.

## The Problem

`test/playwright/e2e/grid/TreeBigData.spec.mjs` has 5 arms. **3 fail, 2 pass**, and the split is not arbitrary:

| arm | line | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Expand / Collapse node via clicks | 23 | ✅ pass |
| Selection happy path: initial render and after single expand | 48 | ✅ pass |
| Bulk Expand All / Collapse All and mixed interactions | 90 | ❌ fail |
| Filtering | 155 | ❌ fail |
| Selection persists correctly after structural changes | 197 | ❌ fail |

**Every passing arm expands one node by clicking it. Every failing arm expands nodes some other way** — bulk toggle, filter-driven auto-expand of matching parents, or expansion after a structural change. The two failure signatures say the same thing twice:

```
# :197 — the root toggle never leaves the collapsed state
expect(locator).toHaveClass(/is-expanded/) failed
  Locator: locator('.neo-grid-row:visible .neo-tree-toggle').first()
  Received string: "neo-tree-toggle is-collapsed"
  34 × locator resolved to <div class="neo-tree-toggle is-collapsed">

# :155 — the filter runs, but no parent auto-expands, so the row count never moves
expect(locator).not.toHaveCount(10) failed
  Locator: locator('.neo-grid-row:visible')
  24 × locator resolved to 10 elements
```

Interactive single-node expansion works. Programmatic / bulk expansion does not reach the projection.

### This is a regression of a COMPLETED fix

#14854 — *"E2E: TreeGrid BigData structural interactions fail to expand root toggle"* — was closed **COMPLETED** on 2026-07-05. Its body names `TreeBigData.spec.mjs:90` and `:195` (the same arm, now at `:197` after drift) and quotes the failure as *"timed out waiting for `.neo-tree-toggle` to have `/is-expanded/`; received `neo-tree-toggle is-collapsed`"* — the identical assertion and the identical received string measured today.

`Filtering` is worse than a repeat: #14854 lists it among the **passing controls** of that run. It is red now. So the failure set has not merely returned, it has grown by one arm that a COMPLETED ticket certified as green.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/data/TreeStore.mjs` owns the visible projection. Per ADR-era design dialogue (Memory Core, 2026-03-09, session `4518f33d-9b08-4538-b91d-928ce86e05e9`) the store keeps only *visible* nodes in the flat `items` array and `splice`s children in on expand, so the grid's virtual scroller keeps O(1) index math. Anything that fails to reach that splice is invisible to the DOM regardless of the record's `collapsed` flag.
- `collapseAll()` (`src/data/TreeStore.mjs:288`) and `expandAll()` (`:555`) both exist and both take a `silent` flag; `TreeStore.mjs:926` documents the bulk-projection contract they share with `clearFilters`. **The bulk API is present** — this is not the "missing bulk operations" gap discussed in March 2026, which was subsequently implemented. Whether these methods are reached, or reached and not projected, is **not measured here**.
- `src/grid/column/component/Tree.mjs` owns `onToggleClick`, the path the two *passing* arms exercise. That it passes while the bulk paths fail localises the defect away from the click handler.
- The app under test is `examples/grid/treeBigData/index.html` (spec line 16).

## Evidence

Run on `agent/18252-topology-seams` @ `e9dd4c5ed9`, working tree clean — **not** `dev`. That branch is 2 commits ahead of `dev` and touches only `src/dashboard/dock` + `apps/workstation`, nothing in `src/data` or `src/grid`. Stated rather than glossed, because a census is only valid against the tree it ran on.

```bash
npm run test-e2e -- grid/TreeBigData.spec.mjs --reporter=line
# 3 failed, 2 passed (52.4s)
```

The cross-check is what makes the tree question moot: `@neo-opus-vega` independently ran the full tier **twice** — at PR #18249's head and on `origin/dev` — and got the same `:90 :155 :197` signature both times with no rotation. Three runs, two trees, one failure set: deterministic, not flaky.

## The Fix

Not prescribed. The measured facts fix the *question*, not the answer, and prescribing a mechanism from a symptom is how a ticket authorises the wrong fix. The first implementer should start at: **does `expandAll()` mutate the records but never reach the `splice` projection, or is it never called by the demo's bulk control at all?** The `:155` filter arm is the sharpest probe — it needs no toolbar interaction, only a filter that should auto-expand matching parents.

Whoever takes it should also decide whether #14854 deserves reopening rather than this ticket standing alone; that call needs the root cause, so it is deliberately left open here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The root cause is named — which layer drops the bulk/programmatic expansion between the record flag and the visible projection — with a failing-first probe that goes green on the fix.
- [ ] `test/playwright/e2e/grid/TreeBigData.spec.mjs` reports 5/5 on `dev`.
- [ ] The relationship to #14854 is dispositioned in writing: either this is a distinct defect at the same arms, or #14854's fix regressed and the ticket says how it was lost.
- [ ] `Filtering` (`:155`) is covered by the explanation, not merely observed green — it was a passing control in #14854 and its regression must be accounted for, not absorbed.

## Out of Scope

- The other 6 failing arms in Vega's note (`DockSplitterProxyPaintNL`, `WorkstationPaletteBridgeNL`, `WorkstationStarvedGeometryNL`, `WorkstationTabOverflowCapNL`). Different surfaces; they stay with the defect-note until someone reads them.
- **e2e CI topology.** e2e runs in no workflow **by design** — #14685 (CLOSED/COMPLETED) established it, #15110 and #17853 were both closed NOT_PLANNED against that design, and the operator explicitly retired the out-of-CI executor in both repos. Nothing here proposes re-litigating that; the arms being red is the defect, their not being watched is a settled ruling.
- #18246 / PR #18249, which concern how much of the tier is *selected*, not whether the retained arms pass.

## Avoided Traps

- **"9 arms fail and no CI job says so" as one ticket.** The second half is a settled ruling, and filing it would have re-derived it for the third time — `#17853` is my own ticket, closed NOT_PLANNED for exactly that reason. Scoped to the arms alone.
- **Blaming the tier's selection predicate.** The e2e config excludes a spec iff its file text matches `/\bneuralLink\b/` (`test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs:57`). All five failing files lack that token and the four `NL`-named ones destructure only `{page}` — they never request the Brain fixture. The predicate classifies them **correctly**; these are ordinary red arms, not misrouted Brain-dependent ones.
- **Asserting the March "missing `expandAll`/`collapseAll`" gap.** Memory Core surfaces that discussion prominently and it reads as a ready-made cause. Both methods exist on `dev` today. Grepped before writing rather than cited from recall.
